title: Assessing the Reliability of Anomalous Hall Conductivity Extraction in GdAlSi
authors: Anil Kumar, Debapratim Pal, Sudhan Koirala, Muhammad Adnan, Youngsang, Ji, Prakash Regmi, Bailey S. Bouley, Ludi Miao, Yun Suk Eo
abstract: We examine the different methods of extracting the anomalous Hall conductivity using SrRuO$_3$ and GdAlSi. For SrRuO$_3$, where the ordinary Hall background is well defined and the magnetoconductance is small, subtracting the ordinary Hall contribution either before or after conversion from resistivity to conductivity yields nearly identical anomalous Hall conductivities. In GdAlSi, in contrast, the transverse response does not exhibit clear saturation, and both low- and high-field regions can appear approximately linear. We show that different interpretations of these linear regions as the ordinary Hall background, together with the treatment of the measured longitudinal resistance in the resistivity-to-conductivity conversion, can produce completely different estimates of the anomalous Hall conductivity. We also examine whether the nonlinear Hall response can instead be described within an ordinary Hall framework without invoking an anomalous contribution. Our analysis provides practical cautions for extracting excess Hall contributions in quantum materials.
summary: This work critically examines the methods used to extract the anomalous Hall conductivity ($\sigma_{AHE}$) from magnetotransport data in quantum materials. By comparing results from $	ext{SrRuO}_3$ and $	ext{GdAlSi}$, the authors demonstrate that the extraction is highly unreliable if the ordinary Hall background subtraction or the longitudinal transport interpretation is ambiguous. The paper serves as a practical caution regarding the quantitative interpretation of excess Hall effects.
main_problem: The paper assesses the reliability and ambiguity in extracting the anomalous Hall conductivity ($\sigma_{AHE}$) from magnetotransport measurements, particularly when the ordinary Hall background subtraction is non-trivial.
main_result: The extraction of $\sigma_{AHE}$ is highly sensitive to the analysis procedure, especially in materials like GdAlSi where the transverse response lacks clear saturation. Different interpretations of the ordinary Hall background can yield vastly different estimates for $\sigma_{AHE}$.
method: The authors compare multiple theoretical and experimental analysis methods, including low-field vs. high-field fitting, and the conversion between resistivity and conductivity tensors, using the Drude model framework.
model_or_system: The study analyzes magnetotransport measurements in quantum materials, comparing the well-behaved $	ext{SrRuO}_3$ with the more ambiguous $	ext{GdAlSi}$. The analysis relies on extending the single-channel Drude model to account for anomalous and ordinary Hall contributions.
key_observables: Anomalous Hall conductivity ($\sigma_{AHE}$), Ordinary Hall conductivity ($\sigma_O$), longitudinal resistance ($ho_L$), and transverse resistance ($ho_T$) as functions of magnetic field ($B$).
important_parameters: Magnetic field ($B$), carrier density ($n$), and carrier mobility ($\mu$).
main_assumptions: The analysis critically tests assumptions such as the equivalence of OHE subtraction in resistivity vs. conductivity, and the validity of extrapolating low-field linear fits to high fields.
figures_summary: Figures compare $\sigma_{AHE}$ extracted using various low-field analysis methods for GdAlSi, and show finite-element simulations of magnetotransport using the single-channel Drude model.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework using the Drude model for magnetotransport. It then uses $	ext{SrRuO}_3$ as a benchmark to validate extraction techniques. Finally, it applies these techniques to $	ext{GdAlSi}$, systematically comparing multiple low-field and high-field analysis procedures to expose the sources of ambiguity.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter transport, the rigorous mathematical and physical caution regarding model dependence and ambiguity in extracting fundamental quantities (like Berry curvature related terms) is relevant to any field relying on complex measurements or theoretical modeling.
